title: Harbor Payments — integration call notes & next steps
body:
Call date: 2026-03-25
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Harbor PM), Mei Zhou (Harbor Eng), Samir (Harbor Sec), Avery Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood Solutions)
Purpose: kickoff integration for Harbor Payments using Redwood hosted API, confirm requirements, surface gotchas and agree next steps + owners.

Background/context:
- Harbor is a mid-size payments platform moving fraud/risk decisioning partly off their internal stack to Redwood for NLP-based merchant risk scoring and KYC extraction.
- Pilot scope: transactional risk scoring + entity extraction for onboarding flows (approx 200 TPS peak during batch windows; steady-state ~20 TPS).
- Data residency: US and EU; Harbor must keep EU data in EU region.

High-level integration notes:
- Primary integration will be HTTPS REST calls to Redwood hosted API (text->score + structured extraction).
- Auth: Harbor will use per-service API keys stored in their vault; they want RBAC so keys can be rotated per-environment.
- Expected payload: JSON with transaction metadata + customer-provided text (merchant notes). Typical prompt size: 300–800 tokens.
- Response expected: JSON with score (0-1), reason codes, and extracted entities (merchant_name, address, tax_id).

Performance & SLA targets (discussed):
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 180ms for scoring path (they prioritized low latency) — Redwood to confirm achievable with quantized model and prefix caching for common merchant patterns.
- Throughput: pilot peak 200 TPS for short bursts (10–15 min windows). Need burst capacity + autoscale policy.
- Availability: target 99.9% during pilot; enterprise SLA TBD for pilot->prod transition.

Security / Compliance:
- PII: Harbor will redact SSN-like patterns client-side, but still concerned about names/addresses. They want confirmation of at-rest encryption, KMS integration, and ability to exclude logs for specified routes.
- Audit logs: need delivery of request/response hashes (not raw text) to Harbor's SIEM.
- Private deployment? They asked about Redwood Private (VPC) for production if pilot successful; cost question flagged by Alex.

Integration-specific gotchas (from discussion / notes):
- Tokenization differences: Harbor's downstream scoring currently expects UTF-8 char counts. Need to align on tokens vs characters for quota calculations.
- Webhook / retry semantics: Harbor will push back results via webhook to their internal pipeline; need idempotency keys and at-least-once semantics documented.
- Country-specific normalization: extraction for EU address fields requires mapping to local formats — may need custom post-processing or model adapters.
- Rate limiting: Harbor devs will test locally and hit staging; we should ensure their staging keys have elevated burst but are still protected.

Open technical questions (items for follow-up):
- Redwood: confirm p95 latency estimate with the chosen model variant and expected prompt length distribution. (Action: Avery)
- Harbor: provide sample payloads (10 representative transactions across US/EU) and a small golden set for extraction evaluation. (Action: Alex)
- Security: confirm whether Harbor requires full VPC/on-prem for pilot or only for prod. (Action: Samir)
- Logging: agree on hashed request/response format and retention window. (Action: Priya to draft proposal)

Action items & owners (agreed on call):
- Avery: run a quick perf test matrix (model variants + quantization) and share p50/p95/p99 latency with 300/600/800 token prompts by 2026-03-28.
- Jordan: share staging API key + quickstart cURL and Postman collection for Harbor to test by 2026-03-26.
- Alex (Harbor): deliver representative sample dataset (anonymized) and success criteria for extraction by 2026-03-29.
- Priya: prepare security brief (KMS options, log redaction, audit export) and proposed retention defaults by 2026-03-30.
- Samir (Harbor Sec): confirm compliance requirements (any additional certifications needed) by 2026-04-02.

Risks / blockers to watch:
- If EU data residency is required at pilot start, we may need region-specific deployment which could delay pilot. Flag for product/infra.
- If sample payloads include high prompt variance, scoring latency/cost may increase significantly — watch token distribution.

Notes to self (Avery):
- Prepare a short demo script that shows scoring + entity extraction in under 2 minutes for next sync. Include export of hashed logs to Harbor SIEM (mock).
- Draft RBAC guidance for API key rotation + staging allowances.
- Coordinate with infra on EU region readiness; cc: jess@redwood infra lead.

Next sync: weekly standup Tuesdays 11am PT starting 2026-03-31 (tentative) — aim to review perf numbers and sample dataset results.

Misc: Harbor asked about cost ballpark for 200 TPS sustained vs burst — give rough delta (hosted API pricing + reserved capacity notes) but mark as preliminary. Prepare cost sheet if they push to prod.

End notes: keep this doc as the working scratchpad. Convert to more formal onboarding doc once we have perf bake and sample set.
